sources.name: United Arab Emirates · entry requirements
sources.summary: Passport validity at least six months. Carry evidence matching the business visit; paid work or booth installation may require a different permission.

sources.name: Thailand · entry requirements
sources.summary: For the October and November shows use the new 30-day rule, not the former 60-day allowance. Check arrival declaration requirements before departure.

sources.name: Malaysia · entry requirements
sources.summary: Mutual exemption effective 17 July 2025 includes eligible short business visits. Arrival formalities and work restrictions remain separate.

sources.name: Singapore · entry requirements
sources.summary: Chinese ordinary passport holders qualify. Check SG Arrival Card and permitted short business activities separately from paid work.

sources.name: Indonesia · entry requirements
sources.summary: Business exhibition visitors and exhibitors are distinct. Chinese embassy guidance says exhibiting requires C11; do not use a visitor VOA to staff a booth.

sources.name: Russia · entry requirements
sources.summary: The July 2026 notice extends the policy beyond the previously stated September 2026 expiry. Confirm permitted business activities and travel/payment arrangements separately.

sources.name: Japan · entry requirements
sources.summary: Invitation and supporting company documents normally required; apply through the designated channel for your consular district. No approval rate or fixed processing promise is assumed.

sources.name: Morocco · entry requirements
sources.summary: Prepare passport, return travel, accommodation and business invitation evidence. Chinese embassy flags problems on some Schengen transit routes; plan the routing as well as entry.

sources.name: Vietnam · entry requirements
sources.summary: Electronic visa applications are available to all nationalities. Use the official portal and select the actual purpose, entry point and dates; confirm exhibitor/work activities separately.

sources.name: Saudi Arabia · entry requirements
sources.summary: China is on the tourist eVisa eligibility list. That establishes an easy tourism route, not blanket permission for commercial exhibiting; confirm the correct business/event visa for the planned role.

sources.name: United Kingdom · entry requirements
sources.summary: Apply before travel if required. Meetings and conferences are permitted; prepare purpose, funding and return evidence and an event invitation. China ordinary passport baseline does not assume an existing UK visa.

sources.name: United States · entry requirements
sources.summary: Business conferences fall under the visitor route. Application, appointment/interview requirements and eligibility need planning. Check EVUS when using an applicable Chinese 10-year B visa.

sources.name: France · entry requirements
sources.summary: Trade fairs and conferences qualify as business travel. Purpose, finances, travel insurance and application/biometric requirements apply; use the correct main-destination consulate.

sources.name: Germany · entry requirements
sources.summary: German missions in China publish a business-trip checklist. Invitation and employment/financial evidence plus the relevant application formalities are required.

sources.name: Italy · entry requirements
sources.summary: Schengen business route; verify the Italy-specific document checklist and appointment channel for the applicant residence. Country checklist remains to be checked.

sources.name: India · entry requirements
sources.summary: Chinese nationals should follow the Indian mission business visa checklist, including invitation and company evidence. Do not assume general tourist eVisa eligibility covers a trade-fair business trip.

visas.notes: Passport validity at least six months. Carry evidence matching the business visit; paid work or booth installation may require a different permission.

visas.stay: 30 days per visit from 15 Sep 2026; 90/180 cap
visas.notes: For the October and November shows use the new 30-day rule, not the former 60-day allowance. Check arrival declaration requirements before departure.
Mutual exemption effective 17 July 2025 includes eligible short business visits. Arrival formalities and work restrictions remain separate.
Chinese ordinary passport holders qualify. Check SG Arrival Card and permitted short business activities separately from paid work.

visas.route: B1 visitor eVOA; C11 for exhibitors
visas.notes: Business exhibition visitors and exhibitors are distinct. Chinese embassy guidance says exhibiting requires C11; do not use a visitor VOA to staff a booth.

visas.stay: Up to 30 days; exemption extended to 31 Dec 2027
visas.notes: The July 2026 notice extends the policy beyond the previously stated September 2026 expiry. Confirm permitted business activities and travel/payment arrangements separately.
Invitation and supporting company documents normally required; apply through the designated channel for your consular district. No approval rate or fixed processing promise is assumed.
Prepare passport, return travel, accommodation and business invitation evidence. Chinese embassy flags problems on some Schengen transit routes; plan the routing as well as entry.

visas.stay: Up to 90 days, single or multiple entry
visas.notes: Electronic visa applications are available to all nationalities. Use the official portal and select the actual purpose, entry point and dates; confirm exhibitor/work activities separately.

visas.route: Tourist eVisa eligibility; business purpose check
visas.stay: Tourist eVisa up to 90 days; verify granted terms
visas.notes: China is on the tourist eVisa eligibility list. That establishes an easy tourism route, not blanket permission for commercial exhibiting; confirm the correct business/event visa for the planned role.

visas.route: Standard Visitor for permitted business activities
visas.stay: As granted, normally up to six months
visas.notes: Apply before travel if required. Meetings and conferences are permitted; prepare purpose, funding and return evidence and an event invitation. China ordinary passport baseline does not assume an existing UK visa.
Business conferences fall under the visitor route. Application, appointment/interview requirements and eligibility need planning. Check EVUS when using an applicable Chinese 10-year B visa.

visas.stay: Up to 90 days per 180 days, within visa conditions
visas.notes: Trade fairs and conferences qualify as business travel. Purpose, finances, travel insurance and application/biometric requirements apply; use the correct main-destination consulate.

visas.stay: Up to 90 days per 180 days, within visa conditions
visas.notes: German missions in China publish a business-trip checklist. Invitation and employment/financial evidence plus the relevant application formalities are required.

visas.stay: Up to 90 days per 180 days, within visa conditions
visas.notes: Schengen business route; verify the Italy-specific document checklist and appointment channel for the applicant residence. Country checklist remains to be checked.
visas.evidence: General Schengen rule; Italy checklist pending

visas.route: Business visa via Indian mission / authorised channel
visas.notes: Chinese nationals should follow the Indian mission business visa checklist, including invitation and company evidence. Do not assume general tourist eVisa eligibility covers a trade-fair business trip.

method: Public-source research snapshot, not a live feed. Facts are paraphrased extracts; fit and next steps are analyst judgements, not organiser claims. An official date means published, not guaranteed to take place. No global completeness claim. Chinese ordinary passport baseline; no existing foreign visas assumed. Visa difficulty is a planning category, not an approval probability. All dates are local show dates. Booth prices, deadlines, buyer quality and work permissions require separate confirmation.
